rejected.reason: False dependency and chain inheritance. Node n-13-1 is Jowett's self-contained analytical commentary on the mathematical symbolism of 729. It directly analyzes Plato's formula rather than depending on an inferential progression within node n-12-5. Propagating the depth of n-12-5 (2.5) to elevate commentary to depth 3.0 conflates subject matter reference with reasoning prerequisites.

Reversed or unsupported dialectical prerequisite. Node n-14-2 is the commentator's positive exposition of a modern aesthetic theory regarding the mediating function of art. While it responds contextually to Plato's critique (n-14-1), it does not logically depend on the premises of n-14-1 to deduce its conclusion; treating an objection/counter-thesis as incorporating prior depth (2.0 -> 2.5) confuses topical contrast with cumulative reasoning depth.

Unsupported prerequisite dependency. Node n-15-1 assesses Niebuhr's historical objection regarding Plato's Athenian citizenship. It does not require or build upon n-14-7 as an internal inferential prerequisite; rather, it introduces a localized argument on Plato's universal philosophical orientation.

Conflation of subject-matter reference with inferential dependency. Node n-15-2 is Jowett's critical essay introducing the paradox of community of goods and historicizing ancient versus modern conceptions of property. Mentioning Plato's proposal from Book III (n-6-4) does not make n-6-4 a direct reasoning prerequisite that forces n-15-2 to inherit a depth of 2.5.

Conflation of commentary reference with dialectical dependency. Node n-15-4 is the commentator's critical review of Plato's arguments on women's education and civic roles. It summarizes the arguments already made in the text rather than building an inferential step on top of n-7-5, making the depth score of 2.5 and the prerequisite link an artificial chaining of commentary to text.

Conflation of commentary exposition with reasoning prerequisite. Node n-15-5 introduces and examines the second paradox (community of wives and children). It does not inferentially derive its claims from node n-8-1, but rather summarizes and evaluates it from an external perspective; hence assigning prerequisite n-8-1 and depth 2.5 is ungrounded.

Artificial prerequisite and inflated depth. Node n-16-7 comments on the balance of music and gymnastic in early education. It does not logically depend upon n-16-6 (the general life-long turning of the soul) as an inferential prerequisite, nor does the text warrant a depth of 2.5.

Unsupported prerequisite. Node n-17-2 reviews the transition from mathematical studies to dialectic in Plato's curriculum; citing n-16-6 as a formal inferential prerequisite is an ungrounded topical association rather than a strict direct deductive requirement.

Unsupported prerequisite dependency. While n-17-3 discusses lifelong education, it is a freestanding reflection on adult self-education and psychological inertia, not an inferential deduction logically dependent on n-16-6.

Confusion of dramatic/dialectical reflection with cumulative inferential depth. Socrates' recognition of aporia (that by skipping the definition of justice to debate downstream qualities he knows nothing) is a meta-dialogue observation rather than an extended deductive conclusion building cumulatively to depth 3.5 on top of n-21-3.
